routing.reason: A fully specified feature across one small codebase: a new migration, API changes, a new endpoint, a page update, tests and README.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow — a standard feature that needs a plan and the full review chain — cost if wrong: hotfix would skip the plan gate, so nothing is lost here

Ruling: skip the frame (po) step — the ticket has 8 numbered, testable acceptance criteria and the code is small (about 275 lines) — cost if wrong: an edge case (for example an invalid `?tag=` value) is decided by the lead and the reviewer instead of the user

Ruling: no PRD, architect or UX step — the data model is given (own tables, new migration) and the page change is a list of tags plus a filter, in a 36-line HTML page — cost if wrong: the UI may need one revision after the visual review
Ruling: no SEO step — one private task page, no public content — cost if wrong: none expected

Ruling: security review at medium effort — user input is parsed and normalized and SQL queries are built with it, but there is no authentication or personal data; parameterized queries are the main point to check — cost if wrong: a missed injection or an unescaped tag in the page, so the page must not use innerHTML for tags

Ruling: the dba migration review stays on (the diff adds a migration) — it must check the join table with a foreign key `ON DELETE CASCADE` (foreign_keys is already ON in openDb) and that the migration is appended, never edits the shipped one — cost if wrong: orphan links when a task is deleted
Ruling: budget $2 — M size, about 6 files, a plan gate, and the review steps — cost if wrong: the run asks the user before spending more

criteria.why: toTasks adds tags to every task, sorted by name, defaulting to []; tested on create, get and list.
POST and PATCH parse body.tags; PATCH replaces the list only when tags is defined, and tests cover replace, keep and clear.
normalizeTags trims, lowercases and dedupes, then checks the pattern and the 10-tag cap; invalid input gives 400 before any write, with many invalid-case tests.
?tag= is normalized, invalid values give 400, and it combines with done in one query; tests cover both.
listTags joins task_tags, so unused tags are not listed; it is sorted by name and tested through untag and delete.
A new migration adds tags and task_tags with ON DELETE CASCADE; foreign_keys is on, and tests check the link rows and the upgrade of an old DB.
Tags render as buttons, clicking one sets the filter, Show all clears it, and the add form takes comma-separated tags.
The API tests are extensive and the README documents the endpoints and the rules.

findings.what: listTasks changes how ?done= is handled. The old code treated any non-empty value as true. Now only 'true' or 'false' filter and other values are ignored. This is arguably a bug fix, but the ticket doesn't ask for it, and it has no test or README note.
toTasks loads every row of task_tags on each call, even for getTask on a single task or a filtered list. That is O(all links) per request. Filtering by task ids would scale better.
A PATCH with invalid tags on a non-existent task returns 400 instead of 404. Validation runs before the existence check. This is minor and debatable.
The page adds an empty-state message ('No tasks.') and moves focus after the filter changes. Neither is asked for in the ticket. The submit handler also gained a try/catch, which is a reasonable fix.
The ?tag= with ?done=true test and the ?done=false test overlap. The first has a redundant assert (open.id !== done.id). The page's tag UI is not tested, which is understandable given the tooling.
Migration 2 creates three statements in one string, which relies on exec running multiple statements. It works, but the migration list is now less uniform.

judge.summary: The diff meets all eight criteria. It uses a proper migration with cascading link tables, validates before writing, wraps writes in transactions, and has thorough API tests. The deductions are small: an unrequested change to the done= filter semantics, a few extra UI touches, and an inefficient load of all tag links on every task read.
